core.title: Make the URN name segment match the file's basename
core.given: A file carries a URN of the stack's component URN shape and its basename is not one of the stack's structural-role names
core.when: the file's URN and basename are compared
core.then: The URN's component-name segment (the segment that names the component, per the stack's component URN shape) MUST identify the component the file implements and match the file's basename, compared case- and separator-insensitively.
prefer: During GREEN: derive the name from the actual file/component being implemented.
During GREEN: correct a copied or stale URN declaration before considering a file rename.
During GREEN: keep structural-role filenames as structural roles when that is their real responsibility.
avoid: Copy-pasting a URN declaration without updating its name segment.
Renaming a correctly named component merely to preserve a wrong URN.
Using an exempt structural name to evade component identity.
unless: The basename names a structural role rather than a component (the stack's exempt structural names, from the profile): the file assembles rather than implements.
The URN is not of the stack's component URN shape: skipped.
core.why: A URN naming a different component than its file is worse than a missing one: it binds the file's evidence to somebody else's component, so both are wrong and neither is obviously wrong.
evidence: The stack's convention check for this rule reports no finding.
The URN name and implementation identity agree.
verification: A repository-wide static check parses in-scope files for a URN of the stack's component URN shape and compares its name segment with the file basename; it applies to existing files regardless of the current change, and files carrying no such URN are not covered.

Both the name segment and the file basename are normalised to lowercase alphanumerics (ignoring case and all non-alphanumerics) before comparison, so a name differing only by case or separators matches.
The name segment is the component-name segment defined by the stack's component URN shape.
Basenames that name a structural role rather than a component are exempt; the exempt set is stack data taken from the profile.
A URN that does not have the stack's component URN shape is skipped, not reported.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: file carrying a URN of the stack's component URN shape
file whose basename is not one of the stack's structural-role names

fires: A file carries a component URN whose name segment names a different component than the file's basename (e.g. a URN declaration copied from a sibling file).
An existing file, not touched in the current change, carries a component URN whose name segment does not match its non-exempt basename after normalisation.
doesNotFire: The name segment differs from the basename only by case or non-alphanumerics (e.g. a separator-cased basename with a differently-cased name segment).
The file's basename is an exempt structural-role name.
The URN is not of the stack's component URN shape (the check is skipped).

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape that identifies a component: which URNs this rule scopes to (their segment count) and which segment is the component-name segment that must match the basename.
profileRequirements.bunValue: six-segment URN; the `{Name}` segment is segment 3 of the URN, identifying the component the file implements

profileRequirements.meaning: Basenames that name a structural role rather than a component (the file assembles or wires rather than implements one component); these are exempt from the name-segment match.
profileRequirements.bunValue: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's filenames that name a structural role rather than a component (assembly, wiring, layout, entrypoint); exempt from component-identity checks such as the URN name-segment match.
proposedKeys.bunValue: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.<role>.name holds a single architectural role's local name, and its closed param list cannot express names like wagon, schema, index or http; no existing key holds the one stack-wide list of structural filenames that a component-identity check must exempt.

bunOnly.text: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-004 / BUN-GREEN-URN-NAME-MATCHES-001 finding.
bunOnly.reason: Validator and finding ids name this rule's Bun realization; the core's evidence and verification describe the check generically.

bunOnly.text: Exempt structural basenames: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware. This is the Vite exempt set plus the Bun stack idioms `server`, `routes`, `layout`, `partial`, `fragment`, `middleware`, because a full-stack Bun app's entrypoint is `server.ts` and its htmx fragments are named for their role, not for a component.
bunOnly.reason: The list itself is the stack's structural-name data (carried by the proposed profile key roles.structural_names); its provenance — another stack's set plus this stack's framework idioms (a server-file entrypoint, role-named markup fragments) — has no stack-neutral equivalent.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral. What stayed stack-specific: (1) the exempt structural-name list is stack data (proposed profile key roles.structural_names) and its provenance (another stack's set plus this stack's server-entrypoint and role-named-fragment idioms) is bunOnly; (2) 'six segments' and 'segment 3' are the Bun instance of the component URN shape, carried by urn.component — a stack with a different segment count instantiates the same obligation; (3) bun.json never states the concrete URN binding syntax (e.g. the exact header-comment form), so no binding profile key is claimed — the core keeps 'the file carries a URN of the stack's component URN shape' and its verification states that files are parsed for such a URN and that the check applies to existing files, which is all bun.json asserts; 'header' in prefer[1]/avoid[0] is neutralized to 'URN declaration'; (4) 'During GREEN' and 'behavioral acceptance' are ATDD-loop vocabulary and treated as stack-neutral.
